featured_reviews.name: Asad Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having always wanted to visit Lucky Restaurant, the legendary Bandra West institution famous for a Biryani so iconic it is famously loved by actor Salman Khan’s family, I was thrilled to try their brand-new branch in Goregaon East.
We started with the Chicken Manchow Soup, which was served remarkably hot and tasted fantastic with a rich, delicious, masala-based flavor, though a few unblended chunks occasionally disrupted the texture. Unfortunately, the Prawns Chilly starter was a letdown, featuring tiny, chewy prawns and an average sauce that we ultimately couldn't finish.
However, the highly anticipated Chicken Biryani completely redeemed the meal. It was absolutely perfect, boasting a flawless blend of spices, tender meat, and a delicious accompanying raita that made the whole visit worthwhile. We wrapped up with the Apricot Delight dessert, which was spectacularly flavorful and highly recommended.
Across the board, the portions were much larger than expected, justifying the slightly expensive pricing, and the service from the super nice staff was excellent. My only critique is that they should expand their soft drink menu beyond standard Pepsi and Coca-Cola to include options like Campa, Big Cola, and Lahori to better complement their heavy, flavorful dishes.

featured_reviews.name: bhushan bowlekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paying ₹710 for this oily, pathetic dish is honestly shocking.

Ordered Lollipop Khepsa from Lucky Restaurant today, and honestly, it was one of the worst food experiences I've had.
The dish was drowning in oil. My hands were literally covered with oil while eating, and even my throat got irritated afterward.
When I called the restaurant, instead of taking responsibility, they simply said, "Utna to hota hi hai" and started giving excuses.
This is not Khepsa — it's just oily fried rice loaded with excessive oil. The quality was terrible, the taste was disappointing, and the amount of oil used was ridiculous.
Extremely frustrated and disappointed. If this is the standard of food being served, customers deserve much better. Not recommended at all.

featured_reviews.name: Iqra Memon
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience at Lucky Restaurant. The food was not up to the mark. We ordered Chicken Tikka, but the gravy served did not seem like Chicken Tikka at all. When we brought this to the staff's attention, they agreed to change it and suggested that we try Chicken Matka instead. However, it appeared that they simply reheated the same gravy, added some butter on top, and served it again.
The service was equally disappointing. We requested a tissue refill four separate times, but no one seemed concerned enough to attend to it. The staff appeared inactive and inattentive throughout our visit.
Overall, both the food quality and service fell far below expectations. I hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and works on improving these aspects.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently dined at Lucky Restaurant and it turned out to be a delightful culinary experience.

We ordered the half Murg Mussallam, which came with two rich and flavorful gravies – one a vibrant yellow and the other a deep red. The dish was generously topped with juicy tandoori chicken pieces, making it both unique and hearty. Paired with butter garlic naan, the meal was absolutely satisfying and more than enough for two people.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian pudding, which was a real highlight – rich, creamy, and beautifully balanced in flavor. The caramel custard was just as expected – smooth and classic, a comforting end to the meal.

The service was prompt and courteous, and the prices were reasonable for the quality and portion size. A special shoutout to the kitchen for the thoughtful preparation and presentation.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for flavorful Non veg Indian dishes and comforting desserts in a relaxed setting.

featured_reviews.name: minakshi sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
We have been regular customers of Lucky and have always trusted the quality of your food. However, our experience on 3rd January 2026 was extremely disappointing and concerning.

We ordered 1 kg Chicken Biryani, which was delivered hot and consumed immediately. Within two hours, the remaining biryani developed a strong foul smell, and all of us suffered from stomach issues afterward. This clearly indicates a serious lapse in food quality and hygiene, which is unacceptable.

This is the first time we have faced such an issue with Lucky, but it has significantly affected our trust. Serving food that can cause health issues is a serious matter and must be addressed urgently.

I request you to investigate this incident, take strict corrective action, and ensure such negligence does not happen again. I also expect an appropriate response from your side regarding this matter

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our recent visit to Lucky Biryani turned out to be a delicious journey through rich Mughlai flavours, ending with some comforting desserts that rounded off the meal perfectly.

We ordered the Murg Musallam, and it was easily the highlight of our meal. A whole chicken, richly marinated and cooked in a thick, aromatic gravy made with a blend of spices, nuts, and cream – the dish was indulgent, flavorful, and felt true to its royal roots. The chicken was tender, infused with spices, and the gravy was luscious without being overly heavy. The quantity was more than sufficient for two to three people and extremely filling, making it great value for money.

To go along with it, we had Butter Garlic Naan – soft, perfectly cooked with a generous brush of butter and a strong hit of garlic that paired beautifully with the Musallam.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian Pudding, a milk-based sweet that was delicate and smooth, with hints of cardamom and saffron. It was light and refreshing after the rich main course.

We also had the Caramel Custard, which was classic and well-done – creamy, just the right amount of sweetness, and topped with a golden layer of caramel that melted on the tongue.

Overall, Lucky Biryani delivered a satisfying meal – flavour-packed, generously portioned, and rounded off with nostalgic desserts. A great spot if you’re in the mood for classic Mughlai fare done right.

It is very unfortunate to see a place that once maintained such good standards now failing to meet even basic customer expectations. I genuinely hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and works towards improving their service and quality.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
After having a good time at another restaurant, we decided to visit Persia Darbar as one of our friends highly recommended their Murgh lebnani Kebab. To be honest, it turned out to be a great choice.

The Murgh lebnani Kebab was really good. The chicken pieces were very soft, juicy, and perfectly cooked. The flavor was mild and creamy rather than spicy, which made it enjoyable for everyone at the table.

Along with that, we ordered a gravy dish with rumali roti. Since I wanted to avoid gluten, I opted for rice instead. The food was satisfying, and the portions were decent.

We chose to sit on the upper floor, where there is ample seating available. The restaurant has seating arrangements on both levels, and the overall atmosphere was comfortable. The staff were polite, cooperative, and attentive throughout our visit.

Overall, it was a pleasant dining experience with good food, comfortable seating, and friendly service. I would definitely recommend trying their Murgh Malai Kebab.

featured_reviews.name: Carl Rebello
featured_reviews.review_text:
Always been a go to place of mine whenever the craving arises.

On this particular visit was craving for kabsa so when we got there we were seated and after speaking to the staff, we finally agreed to order the Raan mutton biryani. They did constantly tell us that it's generally for 5-6 people and since we were 3 they were suggesting something a bit smaller but we went ahead with it.

The food did take a little while to come but that's understandable and even more so after seeing the massive plate that came onto the table.

The rice was cooked to perfection, the mutton was tender and falling off the bone, the masala was delicious. Overall that dish was the highlight of my day. Trust me when I say I was so satisfied and so grateful that we ordered the dish. We needed to pack more than half of it as it was actually a massive amount of food.

For dessert we ordered the Turkish Milk Cake as I've had almost all of their other desserts before, it was nice and the sponge was very soft and absorbed all the milk and syrup well. It was good but not their best desserts, their arabic custard is a way better option but this was nice to try something different as well.

Lastly the staff are amazing and very helpful with suggestions and also very quick and attentive.

Overall a must must visit.

Their CHICKEN SUFIYANI THAAL is especially impressive—perfectly cooked rice, tender meat, and a well-balanced blend of spices that’s neither too oily nor overpowering. The gravies are thick, creamy, and comforting, pairing well with naan or roti.

featured_reviews.name: Amol Surve
featured_reviews.review_text:
Persia Darbar. From the name itself it sounds like an off shoot of the Persian Darbar and as per their menu too they do trace their to Persian Darbar. However, there’s a huge difference between both.
The food is amazing tbh, oily, but amazing.
We tried the Chicken Butter Garlic, Kebab Platter and the Chilly Cheese Garlic Naan to start with. All top notch I must say, the flavours, cooked to perfection and one of the best cheese naans I had.

For mains we had the Chicken Kepsa Biryani, some naans along with the tava bheja and the chicken lababdaar again, really good stuff.
If you are looking for a place that has really good mughlai food, Persia Darbar is the place. What sets them apart from Persian Darbar is the quantity, and of course the amount of oil that goes in the food, I mean the food here is really oily when compared to Persian Darbar, but barring that, I don’t see much difference. The food is good, the quantity is aplenty and the there’s some real value for money when it comes to the pricing. Just one complaint. The service, that is something they need to improve on, apart from that the place is pretty topnotch

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Maharajas is located right in front of Toyota showroom Link Road Malad West.

The restaurant is decent in size with ground and first floor seatings available. As the name suggests they have tried to create royal ambiance with frames on the wall and some of the pictures were creative too. They can accomplish all size of groups and overall the vibe of this place is nice.

They specialise in Mughlai food and hence you will find kebabs, curries and biryanis in their menu. However they have naan sliders, burgers and other items as well. Loved the menu as it has options for both vegetarians and non vegetarians. The best part which I personally liked is the pricing here as the prices are not too high and the quantity served is amazing.

Went here for lunch and the kitchen service was on time plus the table service by staff Rostan was great.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Lasuni Chicken -
Juicy chicken tikkas topped done in green masala topped with fried garlic tasted excellent. Loved the spice level and the taste of garlic in this as it didn’t leave any strong flavours.

Rozali Kebab -
Chicken roulade filled with chicken kheema topped with cheese was delicious. Loved the grilling here and the chicken had nice amount of garlic ginger used and the cheese adds nice touch to the kebabs.

MAINS~
Butter Chicken.
Mutton Nihari.
Both the gravies were tasty. Mutton nihari was eaten by my wife and her sister and they totally loved it. The mutton was juicy and tender in the gravy so full marks from them. The butter chicken was perfect as it didn’t had excess tanginess of tomatoes and it had nice smoky flavours and it was not too sweet as well.

Dal Makhani -
Very few places nail the dal makhani and Maharajas certainly makes one of the best dal makhani. Super creamy, thick in texture and tasty to the core. Loved eating this with butter naan and definitely a must try here.

Veg Shahi Biryani -
Again a very nice tasting biryani primarily due to the perfect rice masala ratio. The veggies in this had nice crunch and it had paneer pieces too. They didn’t used excess spices and it was just perfect.

BEVERAGE~
Peach Ice Tea -
A great refreshing tea and it went well with the food.

So our meal at Maharajas Malad was perfect in every manner. Loved the outlet, the food, pricing, quantity and service everything is just right. Therefore do visit them.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Maharajas exceeded our expectations with its delicious food, and warm ambiance. It looks like a small place from outside but ambience is welcoming and the place is well decorated from inside.

Butter Chicken Slider bomb: Those were creamy and filled with minced tender chicken pieces and a delightful balance of spices.
The name was a bit confusing as this doesn't contain actual butter chicken.

Chicken Reshmi Kebab: Melt-in-your-mouth goodness, showcasing juicy chicken marinated to perfection with mild, aromatic flavors. Though presentation could have been better.

Mutton Dum Biryani: Fragrant and flavorful, the rice and tender mutton paired beautifully, making it a star dish. I liked it as it wasn't very spicy yet full of flavours.

Fresh Lime Soda: Refreshing and a perfect palate cleanser.

Excellent service was provided by Mr. Sadiq, who ensured a seamless dining experience.

The elegant setting, attentive staff, and authentic flavors make Maharajas an attractive spot for indian food lovers.
I hope they will expand their menu in future. Would definitely like to visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Gurpreet Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The delivery management at this restaurant is extremely disappointing. I placed an order through Swiggy, and even after an hour, the status still showed "Preparing."

When I called the restaurant to check on the order, they seemed completely unaware of it and admitted that the food had not even been started. To make matters worse, when I asked to speak with a manager, the call was disconnected, and all subsequent calls went unanswered.

Delays can happen, but the lack of communication, accountability, and basic customer service was unacceptable. This was a very frustrating experience.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Maharajas offers a mixed dining experience with some hits and misses. The Butter Chicken Naans were a creative attempt but fell short due to dryness. While the filling was adequate, they lacked the moisture and vibrance that a drizzle of gravy could have easily provided. On the other hand, the Chicken Reshmi Kabab was a bit of a disappointment—soft, but tasting bland, almost like boiled chicken without the expected marination punch.

The Mutton Dum Biryani was an absolute delight—aromatic, flavorful, and generously portioned. It was a 5/5 and is a must-try for biryani lovers. To complement the meal, the Fresh Lime Soda proved to be a refreshing choice that paired well with the rich dishes.

The restaurant itself is a cozy spot that surprises with its spacious and welcoming ambiance despite its compact exterior. Sadiq, our host, added a warm touch to the service, making the experience pleasant. Convenient parking along the link road is another plus point. Overall, Maharajas has potential, but fine-tuning some dishes could elevate it to the next level.

featured_reviews.review_text: A gr8 for ur tastebuds around Link Road malad, heard of this place a lot from friend and finally decided to hit…Ordered mutton bhuna and a non veg thali, the taste of bhuna was on point, and they got some kebab in Thali which was crazy stuff and a budget place with Gr8 ambience…although was empty when I visited but I hope this place thrive coz of taste they provide😋😋😋

featured_reviews.review_text:

The kababs are a highlight, grilled to perfection and bursting with spices. Each bite is juicy and flavorful, making them an ideal accompaniment to the biryani.

Desert experience.
Ended the great meal with Gajar ka halwa. It was so freshly made and balancing the natural sweetness of the carrots with creamy and nutty undertones.

The ambiance of the restaurant is warm and inviting, making it a great spot for a hearty meal. Overall, Maharajas Restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Indian cuisine.

Being a pure vegetarian and a big Punjabi food lover, I was honestly surprised by how much I enjoyed my experience at this restaurant. Though they are famous for their non-veg dishes, the vegetarian Punjabi food served here was absolutely outstanding and full of authentic flavours.

The ambience was lively, clean, and very welcoming for families. The staff was polite, attentive, and helped us choose the best dishes according to our taste. The food arrived fresh, hot, and beautifully presented.

I specially loved the Paneer Butter Masala, Dal Makhani, and Garlic Butter Naan — rich, creamy, and perfectly balanced in taste. The Punjabi flavours felt truly authentic, just like homemade North Indian food with restaurant-style perfection. Even the starters and mocktails were excellent.

What impressed me the most was that despite being a restaurant known for non-veg food, they maintained great quality and taste in their vegetarian preparations too. The portions were generous and completely worth the price.

Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience with delicious food, good hygiene, quick service, and a warm atmosphere. Highly recommended for both vegetarian and non-vegetarian food lovers. Definitely deserving of a 5-star rating. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered a boneless mutton biryani, on 8th march 2026 afternoon ,and what arrived was a huge disappointment. This was nowhere close to what a proper biryani should be.

Instead of real boneless mutton pieces, the dish contained tiny scraps of meat, as if the leftovers had been thrown in. The rice had no aroma, no flavour, and none of the whole spices that make a biryani special. There were no visible cardamom, cloves, bay leaves, or any sign of proper seasoning—just a bland, overcooked mixture.

What I received was essentially a gooey mash of rice and gravy, lacking the distinct layers, texture, and fragrance that define a good biryani. It felt careless and poorly prepared, especially considering the price charged.

A biryani should be fragrant, well-spiced, and generous with quality meat. Sadly, this was the complete opposite. Very disappointing experience and definitely not something I would recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Riyal Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited this restaurant primarily for the experience, and while the ambiance was acceptable, the food quality was an extremely mixed bag across the menu.
The core barbeque items were of good quality, but the overall flavor was quite mild and low on spices. The starters were just okay. For the mains, we had big inconsistencies: the biryani was unfortunately bland, which was a huge disappointment, but the pasta and pizza were great, with the Alfredo pasta being a definite highlight!
The dessert section was the weakest part. The main desserts were not sweet enough as they should be. The self-scoop ice cream was okay, but the accompanying chocolate syrup was thick and hard to spread, creating unnecessary difficulty.
In summary: Coming here for the experience once is okay, but based on the overall mixed quality and the disappointing desserts, I don't think a return visit would be a good idea.
